method: The Van Slyke and Price formula predicts rennet-set cheese yield from the fat and casein of the milk and the moisture the cheese is made to: kilograms of cheese per 100 kg of milk are (0.93 × fat + casein − 0.1) × 1.09 ÷ (1 − moisture). The 0.93 keeps 93 percent of the milk fat in the cheese, the 0.1 kg per 100 kg is the casein lost in the whey as glycomacropeptide, and 1.09 adds the salt, milk salts and lactose that stay in the curd, about nine percent of its fat and casein, while the moisture fraction divides those solids up into cheese. Casein is estimated from the total protein an analyzer reports at the common casein number of 0.78, by the 0.830 × protein − 0.199 regression from the 1998 Ontario bulk-tank survey, or typed directly from a casein-calibrated test. Fat is limited to 0 to 12 percent, protein to 0.1 to 10 percent, casein to 0 to 9 percent and target cheese moisture to 20 to 60 percent, and casein has to stay above the 0.1 kg lost in the whey. The result is a theoretical target for Cheddar and Colby-style makes, not a guarantee: pasteurisation heat, whey protein in the vat, draining pH, curd fines and salt move the real yield by a few percent. Nothing is uploaded, stored or sent.
